content:
maria: quick sync — thinking about routing economics + fanout guardrails. recent canary showed cost spike when heavy gold-tenant traffic hedged to 4 replicas. how do we prevent runaway fanout without shaving SLOs?

alex: ugh yeah saw that. short answer: cap fanout + dynamic score penalty. but the devil is in the policy surface and observability.

sam: agree. options: 1) hard cap per-tenant (fast, simple but can harm latency), 2) soft penalty that increases cost weight (better QoS but needs throttles), 3) admission control that drops/queues low-value requests.

jia: can we be more granular than tenant? e.g., route by route or intent label so PLs can opt in for higher cost? also consider cache-hit amplification — some requests could be answered from prefix cache and not need fanout.

devon: +1 for route-level controls. Proposal sketch: default cap_fanout=2 for hosted tier, gold tenants can request higher via quota. Also add "budget_window" that limits cumulative extra replicas per minute.

maria: sketch of policy DSL I had in mind:
```
policy {
  target: route
  prefer: low_latency if sla == "gold"
  cap_fanout: 2
  extra_replica_budget: 120/sec
  fallback: model-small
}
```

alex: that looks fine. two concerns: 1) enforcement point (sidecar vs central chooser?) and 2) metric hygiene — we need cost_per_request and fanout_ratio exposed by model variant.

sam: enforcement should be at the chooser to avoid RPC roundtrips. sidecar can provide local hints (cache hits) but central decision needs safety checks. ops-bot: deploy-note: "canary routing-change rolled to 5% — monitoring hooks enabled" :eyes:

jia: telemetry additions: add p95_latency_by_route, cost_delta_vs_baseline, replicas_per_request_hist, and a small probe to validate fallback correctness. Also add an alert if average replicas_per_request > cap_fanout * 1.2 for 5m.

devon: rollout plan idea: implement policy compile-time check + runtime enforcement with feature flag. Phase 1: soft penalties (no hard cap) at 10% traffic; Phase 2: gated hard cap at 1% then 10% then 100%.

maria: operational playbook notes — if cost spike detected: 1) flip soft-penalty to hard cap for offending tenants, 2) throttle hedging for probe-heavy routes, 3) rollback policy hot-reload. Keep runbook short.

alex: question — hedging vs hedged-then-cache: should we prefer single-probe + short-hedge when cache_miss_rate > X? might reduce duplicate compute.

jia: yes. add a probe strategy: if prefix_cache_hit_rate > 0.3 then avoid hedging; else allow 1 extra replica only. config: `hedge_threshold = 0.3`

sam: small perf note — controlling fanout also reduces tail variance; but watch out for SLO regressions on gold tenants. need rollback safe guards and canary dashboards.

maria: action items: @alex implement runtime guard + metric emission (replicas_per_request), @jia add probe and cache hints to telemetry, @devon wire feature flag rollout + playbook, @sam prepare canary dashboards. I'll follow up with a short RFC for the policy DSL and enforcement contract.

ops-bot: reminder: incident channel has historical thread 4620005678 about graceful degrade patterns.

alex: noted. i'll start a draft PR for chooser enforcement.

sam: i'll build the dashboard tiles and add an alert template.

maria: thanks all — want a brief check-in Wednesday 10am to confirm telemetry and first soft-penalty canary. :thumbsup:
